A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMDA for multimodal face anti-spoofing. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable and matchable despite substantial rewriting and reformatting. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original MMDA benchmark results, component ablations, depth analyses and feature visualizations in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and additionally reports embedding diagnostics and a pairing-swap analysis in Table 6.

M1.justification: The stated frozen CLIP image encoder becomes fine-tuned in v2. RS2 changes from minimum cosine distance over all text embeddings to half-cosine distance over same-class embeddings. U-DSA is specified as using MoE rather than MLP modules, although MoE already appeared in v1's ablations and conclusion.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WMCA, CeFA, PADISI and SURF under complete-modality, missing-modality and limited-source scenarios. The added embedding and pairing diagnostics do not document additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main baselines in Tables 1–3 and component comparisons in Tables 4–5 are retained. New Table 6 compares the proposed same-domain pairing against random and cross-domain pairing, adding comparison variants within the mechanism analysis.

E3.justification: Reported training changes from batch size 24 and 80 epochs to batch size 576 and 100 epochs, alongside image-encoder fine-tuning. The new pairing analysis holds each input fixed while varying its partner and evaluates residual stability, decision stability and domain dependence. Existing benchmark splits and HTER/AUC metrics remain unchanged; rerunning the retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused mechanism diagnostics: ANOVA-style mean-shift and distance analyses in the introduction, plus pairing-swap tests and domain-dependence measurements in Section 4.3/Table 6. Existing component ablations, depth/caption analyses and t-SNE visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 reports ten pairing repetitions per input and within-swap residual/logit variances. Its introduction also reports separated bootstrap confidence intervals for within-domain versus cross-domain distances, without numerical interval endpoints. Neither version reports seed-based uncertainty for the main HTER/AUC comparisons.

E6.justification: All MMDA benchmark scores and Tables 2–5 remain unchanged. Table 1 corrects MMDG's average HTER/AUC from 22.93/84.19 to 19.24/87.96. The prose corrects comparisons to use the already-present DADM baseline and fixes HTER/AUC mislabeling. New diagnostic results include Table 6's pairing variances and an HSIC decrease from 1.596 to 0.269.

T1.justification: v2 introduces domain–modality groups and the additive decomposition h(x)=s(x,y)+Delta_g+epsilon, and revises the mathematical definition of RS2 distance. These are limited formal additions and revisions. Despite a new contribution claim about tightening generalization bounds, no bound, theorem or proof is presented.

C1.justification: The central MMDA components and state-of-the-art empirical claim remain. v2 adds a substantive claim that MD2A theoretically tightens the multimodal generalization-error bound, although the claimed result is not supplied. The 'purify then guide' framing largely restates the existing denoising-before-alignment contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets MD2A as suppressing group-shared additive nuisance and uses pairing stability and reduced domain dependence to argue against arbitrary semantic subtraction. It attributes missing-IR compensation to the remaining RGB and DEPTH streams, replacing v1's RGB/IR interchangeability explanation. The MoE optimization limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 specifies CLIP ViT-B/16, the differential-attention lambda parameterization with layer index 14, smoothing epsilon 0.2, and pairing during inference. It provides a repository URL instead of promising future code. Conversely, v1's test-HTER-based early-exit selection rule and explicit count of ten caption sets are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including InstructFLIP, CM-CLIP and PA-FAS, while removing SimMMDG and the multimodal parameter-efficient-tuning study. It explicitly acknowledges MMDG as prior multimodal domain-generalization work and positions MMDA as extending that direction through representation-space methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, experimental discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten around 'purify then guide.' The title and author information change, related work is refocused on CLIP-based FAS, and experiments gain a dedicated setup subsection.

P2.justification: The paper adopts a substantially different template, typography, margins and running headers. Algorithm 1 becomes a full-width display; figures and tables are extensively rearranged, including side-by-side visualization pairs. Figures 1–2 receive legend, annotation and caption changes, and Table 6 is added. Figures 3–6 retain their underlying plots.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition, corrects baseline comparisons and adds useful mechanism evidence. However, it introduces an unsupported theoretical-bound claim and retains all MMDA scores despite substantial changes to the stated method and training settings. The PDFs do not explain whether these changes correct earlier documentation or describe different experiments. These gains and unresolved evidence/reproducibility concerns prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
